answer: An agent economy can limit voting power to tokens locked as a deposit, with each token counted only once regardless of how many identities hold it. If a vote is proven to support a fabricated claim, the deposit is slashed and paid to honest agents. Creating a thousand sybil accounts therefore adds no influence without more stake; the attacker must risk real capital and lose its use while locked. Like pigment spreading through an ocean inlet, identities can disperse, but they cannot multiply the backing.
